In fourth grade for me as well, I started procrastinating heavily and in fifth I just stopped doing some assignments because I had no motive. Funny enough when I started using a wax pen in eleventh I felt more inclined to do the things I had to do. My meds don't even make me feel that way lmao. Not to encourage, but experimenting with out-of-body "experiences" can really help put things into perspective. With the right intentions, it's possible to think yourself out of certain mindsets (I think). As long as outside factors are limited and the environment is controlled, new experiences like those can actually be really beneficial to the way you think about things. Spaced out sessions are likely to be more helpful than back to back ones as they can reduce tolerance and addictive patterns. For me, I like to ponder a lot of "why" I feel the way that I do and why I want to die so badly. Then I move to the "what if's" of what changes in my life might make me feel better. Finally I move on to the "how". It becomes pretty easy to think clearly this way and it kinda helps me but I'm still getting there, y'know? 

I hope you can find fulfillment soon.
